note: A 34-page Mars-colony paper - ten-parameter society model, AHP weights, a hundred-year agent simulation of 10000 migrants, an equilibrium search over minimum wage and parental leave, a migration-plan comparison - with 25 printed figures and 8 printed tables, and almost nothing drawn for print. Nine figures are histograms, three are composite panels and seven are drawings, and the tool provenance shows in every one: Figure 1 is a Word hierarchy still carrying eleven blue text-selection highlights, Figure 2 is a word-cloud export, Figures 4-11 are untuned plotting defaults whose y ticks print at about 4 pt, Figures 12/15/17/19-21/24-25 are spreadsheet and plotting exports, and Figures 13/16/18 are pasted shape diagrams, while Figure 3 still shows its editor grid. Caption side is uniform and mirrors the sibling paper one row up the queue in reverse: all 25 figure captions below, all table captions above. Eleven captions cannot be read from the text layer at all, because each pair of side-by-side captions prints interleaved across the two columns it sits under, so those rows are typed from the crop. Four figures are never cited by number (10 and 11 in a sentence that does not name them, 14 and 16 not even by deixis), Figure 23 is cited a page after it prints, and the paper mis-references one exhibit outright: p16 calls the class-transition chart Table 5, which is the income-distribution grid printed under that sentence. Three printed tables - Tables 2 and 3 at the top of p9, Table 7 on p20 - return no measured region and are declared gaps, and three regions are not exhibits at all: the ICM summary-sheet control block on p1 and the two MATLAB code slabs of the appendix.
rules: Distribution plots carry this paper: nine of the twenty-five figures are histograms, the eight-panel block of Figures 4-11 plus the age distribution of Figure 23 [geometry.family].

Seven figures are drawings rather than plots: four node-link diagrams (Figures 1, 13, 18 and 22), two schematics (Figures 3 and 16) and the word cloud of Figure 2, and the rest of the line and histogram exhibits are tool defaults [geometry.family].

Only four of the twenty-five figures carry more than one panel - Figure 12 with eight, Figures 17, 24 and 25 with three each - while the ten plots printed as five facing pairs on pp11, 15, 17 and 19 stay separate single-panel exhibits [geometry.panel_count].

Five figures print a legend at all and four of them put it inside the frame (Figure 12 keys its series per panel, Figures 19, 24 and 25 carry a bordered key in the top right); only Figure 15 puts its key above the plot area, and the eight-panel distribution block, which needs a key most, prints none [geometry.legend].
Exactly one exhibit is three-dimensional - Figure 17, three perspective panels of stems over a floor plane - and no other figure in the paper carries a third axis [geometry.three_d].
No figure prints a colourbar and no encoding in the paper uses a colour scale; every colour in the exhibits comes from a pasted background, a shape fill or a series line [geometry.colorbar].

Caption side is uniform and splits by exhibit type: all twenty-five figure captions print below their artwork and all five recorded table captions print above their grid, with no exception in the paper [caption.position].
One numbering form covers every exhibit - 'Figure N:' for the figures and 'Table N:' for the tables, number then colon then space - and no other spelling appears anywhere [caption.numbering].

Caption length is decided by caption type, not by exhibit size: fourteen are short labels of four to nine words ('Figure 1: Hierarchy Figure', 'Figure 7: Population Zero: distribution of weekly working hour'), six are sentence captions of 13 to 18 words that state a finding, and the four composite exhibits run 16 to 83 words because each panel has to be named [caption.words].
Twenty-four captions are a single sentence; the exception is Figure 23 at two sentences, and it is also the only caption that explains why the picture looks the way it does [caption.sentences].

Only one caption defines a symbol - 'Table 5: Distribution Of Annual Family Income (Wmin is the minimum wage)' - and it is the paper's only caption-level variable definition; the other four recorded tables leave their symbols to the body text [caption.variables].

Twenty-one of the twenty-five figures are cited by number; the four that are not are Figures 10 and 11, discussed in a sentence that never names them, and Figures 14 and 16, discussed nowhere at all [mention.count].

The lead is normally one page: thirteen figures and two tables are announced the page before they print, six print on the page that announces them, Figure 18 is announced two pages early, Table 1 is announced three pages early, and Figure 23 is cited a page after it prints - the paper's only negative lead [mention.lead_pages].

Citation spellings group by chapter rather than by author: 'Fig.1' to 'Fig.12' carry a stop, 'Fig20' and 'Fig21' drop both the stop and the space, 'Fig.22' to 'Fig.25' restore them, and every table is cited as 'Tab.N' [mention.style].

Four lead grammars: sixteen exhibits are announced with an as-shown-in construction, four with 'FigN shows that ...', one parenthetically ('... among citizens(Fig.13)'), and four have no lead sentence because the exhibit is never cited [mention.lead_pattern].

Rule style follows the table's job, not the author's taste: booktabs for the parameter list and the two data grids (Tables 1, 4 and 8), and three horizontal rules plus a single stub vertical for the two class grids (Tables 5 and 6) [table.rule_style].
Not one recorded table is shaded - no zebra striping and no tinted cell in any of the five - although the pasted spreadsheet capture inside Figure 12 does carry a grey header band [table.zebra].

Only Table 8 merges cells: each outcome name spans its mean and std columns and the stub spans both header rows. Every other grid repeats its label on each row instead, which is why Table 4 prints its tier name fifteen times [table.merged_cells].

Only one grid aligns its figures on a decimal point - Table 4, where every value is padded to three decimals. Table 1 has no free numeric column and Table 8's values are 'm * 10^n' strings centred in their cells, so the paper has exactly one decimal-aligned table [table.decimal_aligned].
One grid prints two header rows (Table 8) and one prints none at all, so Table 6's leading block-label row is counted as its header and the row note records the substitution [table.header_rows].

Units are handled three different ways and no table repeats the choice: Table 1 gives them a dedicated Unit column, Table 5 writes them inside the stub ('Income($)'), and Table 8 writes a magnitude into every cell as 'm * 10^n' rather than stating one exponent in the header [table.units_in_header].

Exhibits are reported from the section that states their numbers: seventeen figure rows and no table sit in a result kind, six figures and four tables in a model kind, and the only solution-kind and evaluation-kind exhibits are Figure 3 and Figure 2 [place.section_kind].

Exhibit size tracks the shape of the data rather than its importance: the parameter table takes half a page (0.495) and the eight-panel composite 0.289, while the twenty-one single-panel exhibits run from 0.03 to 0.14 of a page, the plots that carry the paper's claims sitting at the bottom of that range and the Word hierarchy at the top [place.area_frac].

Placement follows the page rather than the section: fourteen exhibits sit in the top third, nine in the middle and seven in the bottom third, and the bottom group is always the tail of a discussion - five of the seven are cited on the page they print on (Table 5 among them, closing p16) and two are the uncited panels of the p11 block - so a page-foot position marks the end of a section rather than a displaced float [place.page_zone].

Three printed tables have no measured region and are declared gaps rather than patched: Tables 2 and 3 at the top of p9, whose boxes the detector does not return even though Table 4 at the foot of the same page does, and Table 7 on p20 [table.rows].

Eleven captions are reconstructed rather than read, because the text layer interleaves each pair of side-by-side captions and frees their tails - p11's four pairs, p15's pair and p17's pair - so those rows carry typed-from-crop and the row note keeps the failed text-layer form [caption.verbatim].

tables.note: the robustness grid: three noise rows (IP, MW, PLP) plus an unbiased row, against five outcome pairs, each outcome name merged over its mean and std column and the stub '1% noise' merged over both header rows. The only two-header table in the paper and the only one with merged cells. Every cell is centred, so the columns are not decimal-aligned, and each magnitude is written inside its cell as 'm * 10^n' rather than in a shared exponent header. The caption line is the table's own note, naming every parameter and its baseline value, and it prints 'pay.Unbiased' with no space after the stop
